The main-text range coincides with the interaction-term prior it reports, so it may be a description error rather than a changed model; the documents do not settle which. AI domain kept.

rows.R: Figure 3 subgroups are <28 wk and ≥28 wk (102+57 = 159; 99+50 = 149). rows.R: Not a meaningful difference. In this trial randomization occurs at enrollment (protocol 'Enrollment and Randomization': infants randomized once consent is given). Same time origin, interchangeable wording.
rows.evidence: Protocol (supp1) p.3 lines 98-101, p.11 lines 379-392, enrollment/randomization procedure section (lines 309-316); SAP p.7; main PDF p.3-4 (outcome ascertainment, '10 months after enrollment').

The main article also says families were contacted '10 months after enrollment'. Equivalent wording with no change in conduct (L would be non_inconsistency), so excluded per Codebook guidance.

rows.R: Protocol and SAP define GI-3 'at 72 hours after the start of operation'; the article says '72 hours after surgery/operation' throughout without restating the origin. rows.R: Protocol (p.17: cumulative total until 72 h after start of operation) and SAP (p.10-11: total in-hospital opioid consumption up to 72 h) plan a 72-hour window; the article reports postoperative opioid consumption up to 24 h (medians 70.6 vs 45.0 mg OME, n=210 each) in Methods and Table 2. rows.evidence: Main PDF p.4 (secondary outcomes list), p.5 (Results), p.6 Table 2; protocol (joi240139supp1) p.17; SAP p.10-11 (outcome list and schedule table), p.24 shell table 13.16.

Described as substantive_difference; the documents do not show whether this was a documented change. AI domain kept.

rows.R: Article Methods lists 'unplanned readmission within 30 days of surgery' as a tertiary outcome; Table 3 reports 'Unplanned readmission after discharge and within 90 d of operation' 31 (11.1) vs 34 (12.2). Protocol and SAP (incl. shell table 13.23) specify 30 days. Within the article, the window of the reported counts is undetermined.

Changed E from protocol_report to report_internal_inconsistency because the decisive conflict is within the main article; plan documents corroborate 30 days. Rated substantive because a 30- vs 90-day readmission rate are different quantities and the reader cannot tell which the counts represent.

rows.R: Protocol gives ERAS compliance as 'graded proportion e.g. 0-30%; 30-60%; >60% compliant'; the SAP names high/moderate/low without cut points; the eFigure uses low <5/10 (<50%), moderate 5-6, high >=7/10 and states the definitions were not predefined. rows.evidence: Protocol (supp1) p.17-18; SAP p.3 (version history: ERAS subgroup added as omission), p.15; results supplement (supp3) p.2 eFigure and footnote.

The protocol bands were illustrative ('e.g.'), and the eFigure footnote discloses post hoc category definitions, so this is a described, disclosed difference in subgroup categorization rather than a hidden change. Labeled substantive_difference because the categories differ materially; interaction P = .966, so no conclusion depends on it. AI domain kept.

rows.R: eFigure legend says the plotted lines are 99% CI; the caption says the numbers on the right are RRs with 95% CI. The plotted bars visually coincide with the printed intervals (e.g., overall 0.88-1.07; low ERAS 0.49-2.08), and the overall row equals the main-text 95% CI, so the intervals appear to be 95% and the legend mislabelled; SAP planned 99% CIs for subgroups.

So two labels on one figure contradict each other, and the evidence favors 95%. Confirmed. Rated minor because no subgroup inference is drawn (all interaction P > .16), but a reader deriving SEs from the 'stated' level could be off by a factor of 2.576/1.96 = 1.31 (J possible). The plan-level 99% vs reported 95% question is noted but is not this candidate's target. AI domain kept.

rows.R: Table 2 shows EQ-5D-5L day 5 difference -0.057 (95% CI -0.111 to -0.003), P=.04, favoring placebo; Results and Abstract say there was no significant difference in quality of life / in any of the 11 secondary endpoints. Literally inconsistent at the stated 2-sided .05 level. No overall repeated-measures test is reported that the statement might refer to; 1 of 9 unadjusted time points.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p.1 (Abstract), p.5 (Secondary Outcomes text), p.6 Table 2 EQ-5D-5L rows; SAP p.13-14.
rows.rationale: Verified the row: interval excludes 0 and P = .04 < .05. SAP specifies repeated-measures models with time-by-treatment contrasts and no multiplicity adjustment for secondary outcomes, so the blanket statement is not supported by the reported contrasts. Probable rather than confirmed because the authors may have intended an overall-effect judgment that is not reported. Minor: a single nominal P = .04 among 9 unadjusted time points does not change the trial's interpretation. AI domain kept.

rows.R: Primary outcome, CNRT nonabstainers, increased dose vs continuation: Results and eTable 4 give RD 6% (95% CrI 2%-11%). rows.R: Protocol Figure 2 pairs varenicline week-6 response '0.50, 0.40-0.60' with ~Beta(785, 869). That Beta has mean 0.475 and 95% interval about 0.451-0.499, so it does not describe 0.50 (0.40-0.60) (Beta(47.3, 47.3) would). The CNRT response row Beta(193, 210) also has a narrower interval (0.43-0.53) than its printed 0.38-0.58. Simulation-input inconsistency.

rows.rationale: Seeded simulation (random.seed 20241010, 200,000 draws) of beta quantiles: Beta(785,869) mean 0.4746, 2.5%/97.5% = 0.4507/0.4986; Beta(47.3,47.3) 0.4004/0.6003; Beta(193,210) 0.4305/0.5277; the outcome-cell Betas reproduce their printed intervals (e.g., Beta(62.2,21.0) 0.649/0.835). So the response-row parameters do not match their labels. Planning-assumption inconsistency for the power simulation; minor because it affects design assumptions rather than reported results. rows.R: Protocol Table 3, Aim 1: power to detect posterior probability of benefit is 0.948 at 0.80, 0.980 at 0.85, 0.974 at 0.90, 0.963 at 0.95. With the same simulated data sets, power cannot rise as the threshold becomes stricter (0.80 -> 0.85). If simulations were independent, a 0.032 difference is about 3.9 MC SEs (K=1000), so an entry error is likely.
rows.evidence: Protocol p.34 Table 3; p.32-33 (K = 1,000 Monte Carlo simulations).
rows.rationale: Nestedness: {Pr(benefit) >= 0.85} is a subset of {Pr(benefit) >= 0.80}, so with common realizations power must be nonincreasing. Python: SE of the difference = sqrt(0.948*0.052/1000 + 0.980*0.020/1000) = 0.0083; 0.032/0.0083 = 3.86. Every other block in Table 3 decreases monotonically. Probable entry error in a planning table; minor because all values exceed the 0.80 target. AI domain kept.
